newsitem.title: UK: Slide in Dated Brent widens U.S. arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Slide in Dated Brent widens U.S. arbitrage.

text.p: Dated Brent continued its slide versus October paper on Tuesday afternoon, widening Brent's arbitrage to the United States and halting the upwards path of other North Sea crude premiums, traders said.
Dated Brent fell by seven cents to Oct -17 cents, while Oct paper reversed early losses to climb 15 cents to $22.75 per barrel by 1710 GMT. Oct/Nov Brent slipped five cents to close at +60 cents.
"The TI/Brent is starting to improve. Brent is still under pressure from lots of offers, but it can't go out too much further because Brent will sell transatlantic," a trader said.
One Brent cargo nominated from the paper chain on Tuesday was clocked to J.P. Morgan and the other was kept by British Petroleum, their fourth this week.
With the backwardation easing and Brent softer, dealers said the recent recovery of Norwegian differentials may have peaked.
One expected premiums for sweet crude to come off slightly, although there was little evidence of this as Ekofisk traded at Dated +36 cents on Tuesday, slightly above last done.
There were still September loadings of most regional crudes available and most October schedules were due by Friday.
